entries.title: What follows from accepted inputs
entries.body: A decision asks what the current engine can establish from accepted sources under the recorded profile. A prediction is your expectation before running. A proof supports a particular derivation; it does not independently establish that source reports describe the world accurately. Read the claim, inputs, profile and revision together.

examples.source: all $p: member($p, Workshop) & approves(SafetyLead, $p) -> authorized($p, Use, Drill).
examples.explanation: Both conditions must hold for the same person before this rule supplies permission.

entries.title: Not derivable in this workspace
entries.body: A FALSE decision can mean that a positive claim is not derivable from this workspace under its closed-world policy. It does not report an exhaustive search of external reality. Negative conditions may rely on this absence. Repair a missing-evidence problem by obtaining and admitting justified evidence, not by asserting the desired conclusion.

examples.explanation: Without an accepted source or applicable derivation for this pair, the positive claim may be FALSE.

entries.title: Source labels and accepted evidence
entries.body: A source label tells a reader where an accepted statement was said to come from. It is metadata, not an independent verification of that source. Compare the supplied passage, the formal statement and the claim supported by the proof. A source that discusses one object cannot justify silently changing its name to another.

examples.explanation: This statement is about Cart2. Relabeling it as a Cart1 observation changes the claim.

entries.title: Where a model, retriever and reasoner fit
entries.body: A language model can propose an answer or draft an encoding. Retrieval can return source material. A symbolic engine can check a supplied formal claim against accepted knowledge. A reviewed combined workflow assigns separate responsibilities to drafting, source checking, formalization, admission and reasoning; failure at an earlier boundary can survive correct reasoning. The companion’s authored comparisons are illustrations, not live model measurements.

entries.title: Preserving meaning when writing a claim
entries.body: Formalization chooses relations, argument roles, connectives and scope. A statement can compile perfectly while expressing the wrong requirement. Test a proposed encoding with cases that distinguish plausible readings, and compare names and roles with the source. Human review remains responsible for whether the chosen model fits the intended task.

examples.explanation: Ari is in the owner place and Meter7 in the owned place; swapping them changes the relationship.

entries.title: Predicate places and names
entries.body: The KR front end resolves supported predicate names against the committed corpus. Each predicate has a place signature. Positional arguments occupy that order, and named arguments must use supported place names or x1-style positions. A duplicate filled place or an argument beyond the signature is an error. A legal omitted place, including a gap left by named arguments, becomes an unspecified value; it does not search for a matching participant.

examples.source: gives(giver: Ari, gift: Crate7, recipient: Bea).
examples.explanation: The named places make giver, gift and recipient explicit.

entries.title: Compile, preflight, admit, query
entries.body: Compilation resolves and lowers source without admitting it. Structural preflight checks whether a compiled form is structurally usable as an assertion, but does not test every restriction of the current project. Actual admission applies the source to a candidate knowledge state and can refuse derived-only assertions or negative cycles. A query is a separate operation with its own result.

examples.explanation: This count can be a valid query even though it cannot be admitted as an ordinary fact.

entries.title: Sharing a requirement across clauses
entries.body: A repeated free named variable connects one selected entity across clauses within a single ordinary connected region of a statement. Different names permit independent choices. Repetition crossing a negative, tense/deontic, quantified, anonymous-witness or abstraction scope can be refused because the engine will not guess its meaning. Use an explicit supported binder for the intended scope; separate period-terminated statements are independent scopes. Proximity of two records does not create an identity constraint.

examples.explanation: Both clauses must be satisfied by the same value of $p.
This free-name repetition crosses a negative boundary and is refused rather than assigned an implicit reading.
The relative condition belongs to the same selected person who fills the owner place.

entries.title: Combining requirements
entries.body: AND requires both connected conditions. OR permits an alternative. Their consequences depend on variable sharing and quantifier scope as well as the connective itself. Use a one-condition case and a split-identity case to test the intended rule; a happy path with both conditions true cannot distinguish AND from OR. A material conditional A -> B is a formula with the not-A OR B shape. Its truth as a query, its admission as a forward rule, and a derived consequent are different observations.

examples.explanation: Both named approvals are required by this conjunction.

entries.title: Cases that distinguish encodings
entries.body: A useful counterexample makes a wrong encoding disagree with the intended requirement. For a two-review policy, test the checker alone, the reviewer alone, reviews on different objects and both reviews on one object. A failure can reveal missing evidence, an incorrect rule, or a boundary of the operation. Diagnose which one before changing knowledge.

entries.title: Which quantifier depends on which
entries.body: Quantifier scope determines whether witnesses may differ. A computer selected inside a requirement for each person may depend on that person; one computer selected outside can be shared across people. Named variables make intended identity links explicit. Inspect actual compiled structure to compare encodings, without mistaking a valid encoding for a reviewed requirement. Test scope with a split-owner counterexample: one owner per computer does not require a single owner of them all. Shared free-variable factoring stops at lexical scope boundaries; make an intended supported shared scope explicit instead of assuming every repeated spelling is accepted.

examples.explanation: Each computer may have a different owner; this does not require one owner of all computers.

entries.title: What a proof supports
entries.body: A proof is the recorded certificate for a particular claim and input state. It can cite accepted sources and record rule applications, equality or negative dependencies. It is different from the chronology of search and from a source’s truth in the world. After a project changes, a historical proof still concerns its original epoch, revision and profile.

entries.title: Text, identity and independent support
entries.body: Two accepted records can contain the same statement text and still have independent assertion identities and sources. Withdrawing one removes only that support. Identity is scoped to a project epoch; a decimal ID in a detached candidate does not identify the main project’s record. Replacing a source creates new accepted support rather than rewriting old evidence.

entries.title: Separate the assurance boundaries
entries.body: Source accuracy, faithful encoding and implementation behavior are separate obligations. Soundness and completeness are claims about specified formal systems and conditions; they are not synonyms for correct external data or unlimited search. A bounded operation can fail to decide even when a claim has a mathematical answer. State the assumptions and evidence behind an assurance claim, then choose tests that could expose its failure.

entries.title: Decision results and operation failures
entries.body: TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN and RESOURCE_EXCEEDED are logical decision results. UNKNOWN retains the actual engine reason, and resource exhaustion retains the actual resource kind. Compilation errors, refused changes, aborted attempts and unavailable collections have distinct operation results. Do not display an error as FALSE, or an interruption as a completed proof. Certificate-only exhaustion is a reasoning operation failure: the API could not supply a complete certificate, so the UI must not turn that failure into FALSE.

entries.title: Local arithmetic and external compute
entries.body: Supported numeric operations can be evaluated locally when their arguments are usable numbers. A nonnumeric named entity can instead require an external compute capability that this browser does not provide. Enumeration does not dispatch external compute and refuses an incomplete result. Increasing inference depth cannot supply a missing provider or convert an arbitrary name into a number.

examples.explanation: This ground arithmetic test is locally decidable; sum(Label, 2, 3) reaches a different boundary.

entries.title: A bounded inference chain
entries.body: Maximum chain depth limits a particular reasoning search. If the engine reports depth exhaustion, that run has not established a Boolean answer. Raising the limit can finish a short known chain, but is not a general repair for unsupported syntax, missing evidence or unavailable compute. Keep the old run with its original profile when rerunning. Increasing this setting does not increase the fixed formula-work or certificate allowances.

examples.explanation: A shallow profile can prevent the query alive(Nori) from completing this chain.

entries.title: Where an operation actually runs
entries.body: The companion executes the supported KR/source workflow in a browser worker. Native host sort configuration, direct IR integrations, filesystem journals, Redb storage, WASI fuel and memory controls, and external runtime callbacks require their respective host environments. Integrate provides separate local kits for these host capabilities; the browser does not simulate them. Browser depth exhaustion does not demonstrate WASI fuel or memory exhaustion. The browser also enforces shared engine formula-work and certificate-size limits; a fuel outcome therefore need not be a WASI instruction-fuel trap.

entries.title: Acknowledged state and interrupted attempts
entries.body: Cancelling an operation ends that attempt without inventing an outcome or proof. Recovery reconstructs the last acknowledged supported source state; it must not publish a partly applied change. A deliberate rerun creates new evidence. Runtime callbacks, subscriptions, cancellation handles and caches are not durable knowledge and may need host reinstallation after native recovery.

entries.title: Execution history versus proof
entries.body: Execution history records the observed chronology of an operation, including attempts, candidates, failures and bounded omissions. A proof records the successful justification or the actual decision explanation supplied by its API. Moving through an existing recording must not execute the engine again. Operations such as find or scan may provide recorded execution and typed results without a Boolean proof certificate.

entries.title: A refused change preserves the project
entries.body: An admission refusal means the proposed change did not become accepted knowledge. Derived-only relations protect conclusions that should come from rules rather than direct assertions. Negative cycles and query-only forms can be refused for other reasons. Read the typed stage and class, inspect the unchanged accepted state, and repair the proposal at the relevant boundary.

examples.explanation: After this declaration, direct readiness assertions must pass the actual derived-only admission rules.

entries.title: Choosing a useful first project
entries.body: Choose a small decision with identifiable sources, reviewable requirements and a maintainer. Compare the effort of source acquisition, initial encoding, review, change management and regression cases. Model-assisted drafting can reduce some work while adding review obligations; symbolic checks can expose modeled errors while leaving unmodeled ones. Evaluate the proposed workflow with actual tasks before claiming speed, cost or accuracy gains.

entries.title: Unspecified places and existential witnesses
entries.body: An underscore or a legal omitted place becomes the explicit Unspecified value. It is rigid: it does not act as a wildcard for any named participant. Named arguments route filled places but leave gaps unspecified in the same way. Thus a receipt for gives(Ari, Crate7, Bea). does not establish gives(Ari, _, Bea). Use ? for a fresh existential witness when the intended claim requires some participant; use Find to return its actual binding. Each ? is independent. Use a shared named variable when several clauses must refer to the same witness. An unspecified place does not prove that no real-world participant exists.

examples.explanation: With only gives(Ari, Crate7, Bea). accepted, this is FALSE: the unspecified gift is not Crate7.
This legal named-place omission has the same unspecified gift and remains FALSE from that receipt.
This existential claim is TRUE from the receipt; Find returns Crate7 as the gift witness.
An observative leaves its places unspecified; it is not a wildcard search for a named participant.

entries.title: Existential and fixed descriptions
entries.body: Description forms contribute different terms and quantifier structure. An existential description searches for a suitable witness under the query’s scope. A fixed description is not automatically rewritten to any named item with the same predicate. Use supported identity evidence or a correctly scoped existential when that is the intended requirement.

examples.explanation: This asks for a computer witness owned by Ari, rather than assuming a fixed description names an existing inventory constant.

entries.title: Names and accepted equality
entries.body: Different source names are not automatically aliases. An accepted identity statement can connect them, affecting substitution and answer deduplication while preserving independent source records. Generated witness display labels are not stable identity handles and must not be parsed as such. The current answer API exposes terms and origins, not a full public equivalence-class explorer. Identity using = is distinct from exact numeric num_equal and arithmetic comparison; a computed relation does not merge entity identities. Numeric compute forms are query-only where the admission contract requires it.

examples.explanation: This identity can make two otherwise distinct answer names count as one.
This is an exact numeric test, not an instruction to merge two entity names.
Equality is binary; state each reviewed identity separately rather than using a chain.

entries.title: Where an answer witness came from
entries.body: A returned binding includes its variable, displayed logical term and origin. Origins distinguish knowledge-base entities, generated witnesses and existential-import witnesses. Existential witnesses can depend on surrounding universal variables; the rule and compiled scope express those dependencies. The current projection does not supply a complete stable dependency graph, so do not infer edges from generated display names.

examples.source: all $p, $r: member($p, Workshop) & member($r, ReviewTeam) -> gives($p, some computer, $r).
examples.explanation: The existential computer is within the scope of both pair variables.

entries.title: Configuration is part of the question
entries.body: A run profile records strict mode, existential import, materialization and maximum chain depth. Existential import is off by default and can change which witnesses exist; changing it rebuilds accepted source transactionally. Strict mode is prospective for supported admission checks, including configured integrity constraints; it is not a general explicit-contradiction gate. A changed answer-affecting profile creates a new input state; recording detail alone does not.

examples.explanation: With import disabled this universal does not itself require a dog to exist; the supported import profile can add a corresponding witness.

entries.title: Restrictions and additional predications
entries.body: A where-relative restricts the described entity; an also-relative adds the corresponding predication in its supported matrix structure. The relative placeholder it refers to the relevant described entity, with the innermost binding controlling nested uses. A parenthesized relative body that omits its required it reference is refused. Compare actual lowered structure when deciding whether an encoding preserves the intended restriction. After a relative-body equality, an unparenthesized following relative can attach to the equality’s right-hand term. Parenthesizing the equality keeps a following relative at the outer level. There is no outer-it subscript: nested it refers inward, so rewrite requirements that need a different relationship.

examples.explanation: The relative body constrains the computer being described, not an unrelated named object.

examples.source: owns(Ari, some computer where it = TerminalA also broken).
examples.explanation: The trailing also describes the equality’s TerminalA term under the innermost attachment rule.

examples.source: owns(Ari, some computer where (it = TerminalA) also broken).
examples.explanation: Parenthesizing the equality keeps the following also at the outer described computer.
The relative body never refers to its described entity, so it is refused.

entries.title: Event structure and modifier grouping
entries.body: The compiler lowers predication into event and role structure. A modifier chain is not automatically a conjunction of independent claims. The current lowering preserves every unit but flattens grouping beyond head selection: [big red] computer(Workstation7). and big red computer(Workstation7). have identical lowered logic. Brackets can express written grouping without producing a distinct inference meaning here. Compare the real artifacts and this representation limit.

examples.explanation: Compare this modifier structure with big(Crate7) & red(Crate7) instead of assuming they are interchangeable.
The current lowered logic is the same as big red computer(Workstation7).; do not invent a semantic grouping distinction.

entries.title: Time and modal flavors are explicit
entries.body: Past, present, future and deontic forms do not automatically project into bare facts or into each other. A rule must explicitly connect flavors when that is its intended policy. Supported surface order places a temporal prefix before its negative atom, and combined prefix families or prefixing a group can be refused. A must statement is not evidence that the ordinary event already occurred. For example, all $x: past dry($x) -> past ready($x, Paint). preserves Past on both literals; it does not establish bare ready from a past observation.

examples.explanation: This is the supported order for the temporal negative atom; ~past dry(Bench7) is refused.

examples.source: all $x: past dry($x) -> past ready($x, Paint).
examples.explanation: An explicitly admitted historical criterion can derive past readiness. An unmarked readiness query remains a different claim.

entries.title: A proposition can be an argument
entries.body: A fact abstraction packages propositional content as a term, and an event abstraction packages event content. Admitting an outer statement about knowledge or desire does not independently admit the embedded body. Treat the quoted content and the ordinary world-level assertion as different claims. Inspect the compiler for actual structure.

examples.explanation: This knowledge report does not by itself add broken(Pump7) as an independent ordinary assertion.

entries.title: Surface checks and native domain sorts
entries.body: The source front end checks supported terms, predicate signatures and structural combinations. Those checks do not establish that every named constant has the real-world domain role intended by an author. Native sort configuration can add domain constraints through host APIs, but this browser curriculum does not configure sorts using invented predicate declarations. A compiled statement still needs source and meaning review.

entries.title: Complete answer bindings
entries.body: Find returns bindings for the query’s selected variables when enumeration completes. A successful empty result means no answers within the represented domain and supported query, not a failure to run. Relevant unresolved candidates prevent an exhaustive collection from being returned. Returned rows are results; they are not a substitute for recorded execution events.

examples.explanation: The shared variable selects owners satisfying both conditions.

entries.title: Count bindings, not source rows
entries.body: Count measures distinct complete answer bindings under the query, including accepted equality deduplication. It is not the number of assertions, events or printed spellings. Exact-count and no-description forms are query-only in this source workflow. A count is only definitive when its underlying enumeration completes.

examples.explanation: This asks whether exactly two represented computer witnesses satisfy readiness; it is not an admissible inventory observation.

entries.title: Finite values, Empty and unavailable
entries.body: Sum, minimum, maximum and average select one named numeric binding across a complete answer collection. Every selected value must be present, numeric and finite, and the computed result must be finite. Empty remains Empty, including sum; it is not manufactured zero. Missing variables, nonnumeric values, nonfinite inputs or results and incomplete enumeration are unavailable results with actual typed reasons.

examples.explanation: Selecting $amount aggregates quantities; selecting a parcel name does not produce a numeric total.

entries.title: Do not total unfinished answers
entries.body: A collection cannot be called exhaustive while a relevant candidate or domain-closure check is unresolved. Find, count and aggregate preserve that boundary instead of silently presenting partial rows, zero or an Empty aggregate. Diagnose the typed failure: a missing numeric binding needs a different repair from depth exhaustion or unavailable compute. No error message substring is a substitute for the engine’s typed classification.

entries.title: Absence, a denial and NAF
entries.body: An explicit negative source can be admitted and keeps its own assertion identity. A negative query uses the engine’s negation-as-failure semantics, so success from absence is not interchangeable with a citation to an explicit denial. Rules depending on a negative condition can lose support when new positive knowledge arrives. Contradiction scans separately examine represented opposing claims and constraints.

examples.explanation: This may be a retained source assertion; inspect the source record separately from how a negative query is evaluated.

entries.title: Which entities every ranges over
entries.body: A universal query is evaluated over the represented domain under its profile. Import settings and newly admitted entities can change that domain. A result over all listed computers does not independently establish that the inventory contains every physical computer. Domain completeness and absence of a derivation are related but different modeling assumptions.

examples.explanation: Adding an unaudited computer can change this result without changing the readiness policy.

entries.title: Negative dependency cycles
entries.body: Rules with negative conditions need an admissible dependency ordering. A cycle through negation is refused rather than resolved by an arbitrary ordering. The actual stratification report exposes predicate strata and dependency information. Repair a circular default with independently supported positive conditions or a reviewed different policy, not merely renamed predicates.

examples.explanation: Adding a reverse default from not-ready to broken would create a negative cycle.

entries.title: Violations and unresolved checks
entries.body: A contradiction report contains both reported violations and unresolved checks. A clean completed scan requires both collections to be empty. The scan checks represented constraints and opposing claims; it is not unrestricted first-order consistency checking. Findings are supplied as actual report text and gap data, without invented assertion links or proof certificates.

examples.explanation: This disjunctive conclusion registers a constraint; explicitly denying both alternatives for a dog can violate it.

entries.title: Publish a whole successful change
entries.body: A change batch applies ordered assertions and withdrawals to a candidate state and publishes only if the whole batch succeeds. A replacement is a specific withdrawal plus new accepted source. If compilation or admission fails, the acknowledged project survives. Check accepted records and revision after failure; retain the failure record separately from successful knowledge.

entries.title: A candidate is a separate world
entries.body: A hypothetical operation applies an explicit delta and profile to a detached source snapshot. Its epoch, results and assertion identities belong to that candidate. Discard changes nothing in the main project. After a delta preview and confirmation, Apply performs fresh ordinary admission against the matching main base; stale bases require retest and candidate IDs are never transplanted.

entries.title: Evidence is bound to its inputs
entries.body: An epoch identifies a project incarnation and a revision identifies its acknowledged input state. A source or answer-affecting profile change makes older results historical for the current project. Replay retains the original identity and never reruns reasoning. A new deliberate query receives a new run identity even when its answer is unchanged.

entries.title: A diagnostic of actual work
entries.body: Materialization is an execution option, not a permanent certificate of all possible answers. Its report describes the actual work available for the relevant state or last query. Before a query or after a mutation, the report can be empty because saturation information was invalidated. Compare ordinary verdicts and recorded profiles while keeping diagnostic lifecycle separate from source truth. An enabled option may do no saturation for a particular operation. The positive classification certificate example has an empty report under the enabled profile; the actual report, not the toggle, establishes what was materialized.

entries.title: Browser copies and native durability
entries.body: Browser progress and exported evidence are local learning artifacts; storage may be unavailable or cleared. Native hosts can integrate source snapshots, journals, filesystems or database storage such as Redb, each with its own durability and recovery contract. Source-recoverable imports validate schema, identity and source-to-compiled correspondence rather than trusting arbitrary inspected IR. Runtime callbacks and other live host resources are not serialized and require explicit rebind.

entries.title: Formula work, certificate size and recording limits
entries.body: The shared browser/native evaluator allows 1,000,000 formula-node entries per verdict search across its depth passes, with a separate equal allowance for certificate construction. Wide quantifier products can reach this limit without a deep rule chain. Verdict-search exhaustion returns RESOURCE_EXCEEDED with fuel as its kind and indeterminate context. A 100,000-step certificate ceiling or exhausted certificate walk instead refuses the whole certificate as a reasoning error; no partial TRUE/FALSE certificate is published. These fixed engine limits are separate from configurable chain depth, bounded execution recording, browser cancellation and WASI instruction-fuel or memory controls. A truncated recording leaves the underlying reasoning result unchanged. Diagnose the actual boundary, preserve the attempted run, and narrow the question only when that matches the task; a smaller question does not answer the exhausted universal one.

entries.title: Conditional truth and admitted rules
entries.body: A -> B lowers to not-A OR B. Asking that formula as a query can succeed through absence of A without establishing B, and a query does not admit a rule. An admitted supported conditional can supply a forward rule: with A established, modus ponens can derive B. B alone does not establish A; reversing a rule changes its meaning. Classical contraposition relies on classical implication and negation. Here a successful ~A query may use negation as failure, even without a relevant conditional, so read its actual evidence rather than calling it a classical contraposition proof. Retained explicit denials and contradiction scans have their own contracts.

examples.explanation: Compare querying this conditional, querying readiness alone, and admitting the rule with a justified approval premise.

entries.title: Two research perspectives on reasoning systems
entries.body: John McCarthy’s Programs with Common Sense (1959) proposes a system that manipulates formal statements and draws conclusions from supplied premises. Karpas and colleagues’ MRKL Systems (2022) proposes a modular architecture combining neural models with discrete knowledge and reasoning modules. These selected primary sources show that explicit representation and combinations of learning with reasoning are research design choices, not accuracy guarantees. The companion’s reviewed drafting-and-reasoning workflow is one concrete arrangement; it does not represent the whole field. Compare what each proposal stores, learns and checks, then separate the proposal from evidence about an implemented system.

entries.title: Names, variables, strings and statement boundaries
entries.body: A statement ends with a period; predicate calls need parentheses. Lowercase predicate spellings must resolve in the committed vocabulary. Capitalized names, $variables, numbers and quoted strings are different term forms. Decimal digits stay together. Line comments begin with #; block comments use /* and */ and do not nest. Identifier syntax is ASCII, while string payloads can contain Unicode. Supported string escapes are an escaped quote or backslash; a raw newline is not a string escape. Opaque words such as me, this and it_a do not look up a conversational referent or assign themselves from the previous sentence. A name that would collide with one of these terms, such as Me, is refused. Bare reserved words have grammar roles; a longer identifier is not split into a keyword and a suffix.

examples.explanation: Comments do not become assertions; the period terminates the predicate call.
The decimal point belongs to the numeric token; a separate final period terminates the statement.
A quoted Unicode payload is accepted as a constant; it is not parsed as a predicate.
These are opaque terms, not a lookup of the current speaker or a previously mentioned computer.
The variable spelling is preserved; everyday is not split into a keyword and a suffix.
This capitalized name would collide with the opaque me term; choose an unambiguous intended name.
Signed numeric literals are not part of this implemented grammar; do not silently drop the sign to repair the meaning.
A missing period is a compilation failure, not FALSE.
The identifier is lexically whole but is not a supported predicate in this corpus.

entries.title: Existence, definite domains and exact zero
entries.body: some introduces an existential witness; the is a fixed description, not evidence of existence. every ranges over its restrictor, while every the uses an opaque definite-domain restrictor rather than the ordinary predicate inventory. A the ... $name: block substitutes the same fixed description through its body. exactly N counts matching entity witnesses; no is its exact-zero query form, not a durable prohibition. Count forms can compile while actual assertion admission refuses them. Term and block spellings express these choices explicitly; a fractional exact count is not accepted. A negated restrictor such as some ~computer constrains the selected witness, unlike negating the outer predication. exactly N the also counts the opaque definite domain.

examples.explanation: This asks whether zero represented computer witnesses meet readiness; it does not record a prohibition.
The block spelling names the same exact-zero witness condition.
This expresses the zero-count question explicitly.
The opaque definite domain is not automatically populated by ordinary computer observations.
A named block keeps that definite-domain choice explicit.
The block reuses one fixed designator; it does not discover or create a computer.
An exact-count determiner takes a natural-number count, not a fraction.
This is a query-only count over the opaque definite domain, not the ordinary computer inventory.
The block form preserves the definite-domain count choice.
The negation restricts the selected witness; it does not negate the whole readiness claim.

entries.title: Linked restrictor arguments and selected places
entries.body: A restrictor can fill additional predicate places while its bound entity occupies the remaining selected place. Linked positional arguments start after the ordinary bound first place. Descriptions inside linked arguments close inside that restrictor scope; do not move them outside and assume the same witness sharing. A compact .x2 selector puts the bound entity in the second place. The selector must be adjacent to its predicate and does not also take linked arguments. A named it can state the selected bound place in the longer form. Replacing that place with an unrelated fixed argument leaves no place for the bound entity and is refused.

examples.explanation: The quantified entities occupy owns x1; Meter7 fills its linked second place.
The same linked second place is written explicitly.
The computer description is scoped inside the ownership restrictor.
The bound entities occupy owns x2 rather than the first place.
The longer form marks the second place as the bound entity.
A fixed first-place value cannot silently replace the bound entity; use the intended linked or selected place.
Whitespace breaks the compact selector; write the adjacent selector or a supported long form.
A selected compact restrictor cannot also carry linked arguments; rewrite with named places.

entries.title: Attached relations and curated compounds
entries.body: via adds a relation in the current lowering: the supplied tag term fills that relation’s first place, and the main predication’s first argument fills its second place; remaining places are unspecified. It does not link to a reified event identifier. Inspect that actual projection before choosing the form for an intended causal or instrumental claim. Tag syntax accepts one supplied term and requires a predicate with at least two places. A + compound instead names a committed corpus relation with its own place structure. Juxtaposed modifiers remain productive, but plausible uncurated compounds are refused. Replacing a compound with modifiers can change meaning and requires review.

examples.explanation: The current flat cause relation uses the rain witness and Cart7, with its remaining place unspecified; it does not use the readiness event ID.
Inspect the actual uses(Meter7, Cart7, unspecified) projection before claiming this syntax expresses the intended tool relationship.
The unary person relation cannot provide the required two tag places.
A via tag accepts one supplied term, not an ordinary multi-argument call.
This curated compound has a declared relation and place structure; its places are not inferred from the words.
A plausible uncurated compound is refused instead of being interpreted as its final word.
The compound join must be adjacent; spaces do not create an alternative compound syntax.

entries.title: Opaque content kinds and the property slot
entries.body: The implemented abstraction terms distinguish event, fact, property, amount and concept content. Their brace-delimited bodies stay inside the content term; an outer knowledge or desire assertion does not admit the body as an ordinary fact. A property body may use slot for its open place. slot is neither a free named variable nor an independent ? witness, and is refused outside a property body. An amount abstraction is an opaque content kind, not a computed aggregate or measured number. These forms do not supply arbitrary higher-order execution, automatic belief truth or an assignment mechanism.

examples.explanation: The embedded event content is not an independently admitted breakage observation.
The fact-content term remains part of the outer knowledge statement.
The open place belongs to this property content.
An amount-kind content term is not a numeric aggregate result.
The content kind is retained without making the embedded predicate an outer assertion.
There is no property binder for this open place.
A fact abstraction does not bind the property-only slot.

entries.title: Precedence, alternatives and refused negation
entries.body: From tighter to looser, the surface operators are atomic negation, temporal/deontic prefixes, AND &, OR |, XOR ^, biconditional <->, and conditional ->. Implication associates to the right. XOR expresses one alternative rather than both; biconditional connects both directions at the formula level. Parentheses can make a compound grouping explicit. Negation and temporal/deontic prefixes apply only to supported atoms, so ~(A & B), repeated negation prefixes and past (A & B) are refused. Write the supported Boolean expansion when it preserves the intended meaning. Compilation alone does not establish the formula or make every connective shape admissible as a rule.

examples.explanation: AND binds more tightly: the right-hand alternative requires both animal and alive.
The explicit grouping requires alive as well as one of the first two alternatives.
The formula asks for the exclusive alternative, not inclusive OR.
The biconditional is a two-direction formula; inspecting it is separate from admission.
Implication is right-associated: dog implies the animal-implies-alive formula.
A negated compound has no supported direct surface carrier.
This is the supported Boolean expansion of not-both for these atomic claims.
Repeated atomic negation prefixes are not supported syntax.
A temporal prefix cannot wrap the compound sentence directly; qualify intended literals explicitly.

entries.title: Prepare, review, admit
entries.body: PrepareReview validates source bounds, compiles, checks canonical round-trip, renders a deterministic reading and attempts detached admission. Main knowledge is unchanged. AdmitReviewed requires an exact worker-held ticket, unchanged draft and knowledge/profile, and explicit human confirmation; it repeats ordinary admission. A syntax pass is not a finding about source intent. Review is consumed on an admission attempt and lost on worker restart.

PrepareReview { draft } → source, canonical KR, backtranslation, detached admission record

entries.title: Register an existing relation for dispatch
entries.body: CoreSession::register_compute_predicate chooses dispatch for committed vocabulary. It does not declare new words or infer arity. Registering a relation with live stored references is refused because routing would make those rows unreachable. Native callbacks or the component host supply external results. Successful replies belong to one query’s evidence and memo, not the persistent source registry. The browser worker has no asynchronous external-compute bridge.

entries.title: Create, inspect, restore and rebind
entries.body: A session owns its knowledge, settings and source registry. Browser recovery restores acknowledged symbolic state in a new worker; native persistence reopens its authoritative journal. Host callbacks and credentials are not serialized state. Rebind required capabilities after restore. Keep old run records attached to their original epoch/revision instead of replacing their meaning with the current project. Check actual exports before assuming native methods exist in WIT.

examples.explanation: Native compute and scoped-application kits
examples.run_in: Native compute and scoped-application kits

entries.title: Conservative authorization with scoped context
entries.body: The native Authorizer loads a policy, combines durable facts with temporary call context, evaluates an authorization query and clears that temporary context. Its adapter allows only TRUE; FALSE, UNKNOWN and RESOURCE_EXCEEDED do not permit an action. The application must authenticate callers, construct trusted context, select the correct resource and perform any actual side effect. A decision cache is scoped by policy and context; it is not permission to change the resource or reuse obsolete evidence.

entries.title: Import a supported ontology fragment
entries.body: The small native reader accepts a restricted textual format and collapses IRIs to local names. Class/type input changes native sort configuration; ordinary triples become two-place facts. Imports mutate incrementally, so use a disposable candidate and discard it after any failure. The exporter describes an exportable fact fragment, not the original ontology, namespace provenance, rules, or application journal. Inspect its refused list as part of the result.

entries.title: Keep document, assertion and run identities distinct
entries.body: A document ID/revision identifies application evidence. An assertion ID identifies an admitted source in a session. Epoch and revision identify the knowledge used by a run. The companion retains source text and hashes alongside reviewed assertions; those hashes bind bytes but do not authenticate a source or prove an imported review occurred. Withdrawal targets actual assertion IDs. A document edit alone does not silently retract the corresponding accepted premise.

entries.title: Inspect a WIT world and package identity
entries.body: This pin exposes the nibli:engine@0.12.0 interfaces through a component world. Crate version 0.2.0, WIT package version and source commit are distinct identities. The artifact exports engine and authorizer resources and imports compute-backend plus listed WASI facilities. Use the actual extracted world to establish what a host must provide; a source filename is not an interface inspection.

entries.title: Values cross a boundary; resources have an owner
entries.body: WIT records, variants and lists describe values crossing the component boundary. Resources represent owned state with creation, use and release. A host should not keep using a poisoned instance after a trap or treat a resource handle from one instance as a handle in another. Recreate resources and replay acknowledged inputs during recovery. Typed errors returned by a call differ from a host trap that interrupts that call.

trap → discard poisoned instance → recreate resource → replay journal

entries.title: A guest boundary does not erase host capabilities
entries.body: The observed component imports WASI IO, CLI and an insecure random seed alongside compute interfaces. It has no guest filesystem, socket, HTTP or clock import at this pin. Its host still owns files, process state and the loopback compute bridge. A sandbox limits the guest’s route to capabilities; it does not validate returned evidence or authorize host side effects. Keep capability selection and logical entailment as separate checks.

entries.title: Record the component you inspected
entries.body: Capture source/tool versions, component and host hashes, extracted WIT and the actual import/export list. Compare that record with your deployment assumptions. The kit refuses a wrong or dirty engine checkout and rebuilds the host/component from the pin. Artifact inspection supports capability/version claims; it does not establish the correctness of a future provider or the authenticity of a learner-supplied report.

entries.title: Recover the last committed inputs
entries.body: After a host trap, rebuild the poisoned component and replay only journaled mutations. Preserve stable IDs and tombstones so a later retraction reaches the intended source. The lab deliberately deletes a middle ID before reopening. An interrupted query is not a completed proof and is not a journal mutation. Native journal persistence and browser recovery JSON are different mechanisms; test each one you rely on.

entries.title: Invalidate approval when its basis changes
entries.body: The preparation ticket binds original source, formal bytes, provenance, engine, profile and main epoch/revision. Editing the source or draft clears UI approval. An intervening knowledge/profile change disables admission until a new preparation. The worker independently checks and consumes the exact ticket, preventing replay or a modified UI payload from authorizing another draft. Saved drafts can be resumed; approval is never restored from storage.

edit / knowledge change / profile change / worker restart → fresh review

entries.title: Keep provider failure outside the knowledge result
entries.body: The tutor sends one previewed text request, excludes ambient cookies/referrers, rejects redirects, bounds response bytes/time and discards cancelled or stale responses. Keys and replies remain in tab memory. Authentication, rate limit, missing model, malformed output and network/origin failures are transport states, not symbolic FALSE. Model text is untrusted. Browser cancellation does not guarantee provider-side cancellation or a spending limit.

entries.title: Boolean JSONL is a low-assurance backend contract
entries.body: The stock loopback lab uses newline-delimited requests containing a relation and typed arguments. A parseable Boolean is trusted as the answer; malformed text, timeout or an error becomes backend unavailable. The protocol itself does not establish peer identity, input provenance, model version, freshness or replay protection. Build those obligations into a production host contract when needed, and expose failed checks instead of replacing them with a confident Boolean.

examples.explanation: Native TCP and WASI loopback compute experiments
examples.run_in: Native TCP and WASI loopback compute experiments

entries.title: Retain numeric and representation boundaries
entries.body: Finite built-in arithmetic is definitive when its relation holds or fails; the zero-divisor quotient contract is FALSE. A non-finite compiler-shaped numeric group is UNKNOWN/non-finite. Raw flat compute IR may instead reach a host callback, whose refusal is backend unavailable in this kit. Count/aggregate require complete enumeration, and the engine does not dispatch external calls to invent a domain. Validate the exact ingress and backend argument contract.

examples.explanation: Browser compiler and arithmetic activity

entries.title: Depth, fuel, memory and cancellation have different owners
entries.body: Reasoner depth bounds search. Host fuel bounds executed WASM work. Guest memory settings restrict growth and do not shrink an existing allocation or bound whole-process RSS. Browser cancellation interrupts a worker. Preserve the originating layer and actual failure class, then repair that layer’s workload or limit. A retry should have a new result identity; no incomplete trace should masquerade as a completed certificate.

entries.title: Expose collisions, unsupported syntax and export refusals
entries.body: Two different IRIs can collapse onto the same local name. The small reader is not a conforming Turtle validator: [] is accepted as a bare IRI token in the observed pin. The kit exposes and refuses it in its application preflight. Production adapters should use a conforming parser and an explicit supported-fragment mapping. Keep temporal/deontic wrappers, namespace identity, rules and sort declarations out of an allegedly lossless fact-only round-trip claim.

entries.title: A report is supplied evidence
entries.body: The kit records source inventory digest, engine pin, platform/tools, artifact hashes, observations and log hashes. The companion checks structure and expected identities before attaching it. The browser has not rerun the native experiment or authenticated the author. A failed or incompatible report remains useful for diagnosis, but cannot satisfy the matching lab’s completion check. Keep raw logs, assumptions and execution limits with the report.

entries.title: Relevance selects candidates, not premises
entries.body: The companion’s local search ranks distinct matching words. It exposes document identity, case scope, revision and withdrawal. Compare scoped results with all-case and withdrawn controls. A relevant but wrong-case or obsolete record can be harmful input to a formalizer. Selection only copies text into review. Verify the intended meaning and scope before admission; a retrieved instruction is data, not authority over the application.

entries.title: An agent proposal does not authorize execution
entries.body: A model may propose an action or a formal draft. The application must decide what evidence may be admitted, evaluate current authorization and perform any host side effect. Keep document instructions outside the command channel. Scope authorization by actor, action, resource and current context; clear temporary context between calls. A symbolic TRUE is conditional on the policy and accepted premises, not a guarantee that an operational action is safe or correct.

entries.title: Measure the queue before scaling draft production
entries.body: Daily review load is drafts × reviewed fraction × minutes per review / 60. Capacity depends on available reviewer time and a positive review-time estimate. Sampling can estimate error rates but cannot approve the unreviewed remainder. Use the worksheet to identify unreviewed work, then choose an intake bound, staffing plan or reduced scope. Name the source-policy owner and include correction/regression work in the workload.

entries.title: State the measured phase and environment
entries.body: The kit counts successful allocation requests through a Rust System wrapper and records Linux VmRSS separately. Requested bytes include new reallocation sizes, not live or peak bytes. Six explicit phases are timed with Instant. Three repetitions share a process and may be warm. Record toolchain, build, workload, depth, result and proof size. These diagnostic observations do not establish a general performance ranking or equivalence between debug WASI fuel and native time.

entries.title: Price assumptions belong to the learner
entries.body:
The worksheet uses one model request per draft and 30 days per month. You supply the request price; zero is not a claim about current provider pricing. Review labor and maintenance are separate quantities. Add hosting, acquisition, mapping, onboarding, retries, incident response and the consequence of wrong decisions to an adoption plan. Revisit assumptions with a bounded pilot and real workload data.

Training a model and running a trained model are different workloads. Quantization can reduce stored weight size and change runtime requirements and output behavior; it does not remove review or calibration work. Compare the executable, model weights, knowledge data and peak runtime memory separately. A small engine binary does not include the knowledge-acquisition labor or an external model’s memory.

For a fair comparison, hold task, input data, acceptance criteria, hardware, concurrency and failure handling constant; measure cold and warm paths separately.

review load and maintenance hours remain separate

entries.title: Assign ownership across the whole application
entries.body: A small pilot should name the owners of source accuracy, vocabulary/ontology mapping, formal review, backend contracts, host capabilities, policy changes and recovery. Test wrong-but-provable encodings, cross-case evidence, withdrawn support and provider failure. A compiler gate, formal theorem, proof certificate and deployed-system assurance cover different obligations. Expand only after observed benefits justify review and maintenance effort.

entries.title: The compiler has several different boundaries
entries.body: The executable pest grammar recognizes source structure and returns an owned parser tree. The validating emitter resolves vocabulary and places while producing flat predicate, argument and sentence arrays. The semantic compiler resolves scope, closes variables and builds an interned formula tree; flattening produces indexed LogicBuffer nodes. The session then marks registered compute predicates. An unknown dictionary name can parse and still fail emission. Compile inspection can include structural assertion preflight, but actual admission also depends on the current KB and is a separate operation. Locate the first failed boundary before choosing a repair.

examples.explanation: Follow this source through the captured stage selector.

entries.title: Source correspondence uses byte spans
entries.body: A period inside a quoted literal does not end a statement. Parser spans identify exact UTF-8 byte intervals, including punctuation; byte positions are not character counts for non-ASCII input. The browser selects fragments using captured spans and validates slice boundaries. It cannot reconstruct a missing artifact or turn a later source edit into the historical input. A parser recovery result can contain valid earlier statements and errors; the session’s atomic text admission does not commit that partial result.

examples.explanation: Two real statements despite the period inside the literal.

entries.title: Array indices are typed references
entries.body: AstBuffer is an internal Rust interchange with separate arrays for predicates, arguments and sentences. An index is interpreted in its field’s array, not in a universal pool. Public compilation validates reachable index bounds and acyclicity before recursive lowering; DAG sharing is legal. Corrupt hand-built roots and cycles are refused. Parsed debug strings help inspect a run but are not a stable AST wire format. LogicBuffer is the separate flattened representation exported by component interfaces.

examples.explanation: Run real parser, emitter, corrupt-buffer and admission controls.
examples.run_in: Pinned local lab kit inside nix develop

entries.title: Follow meaning through connective lowering
entries.body: The semantic IR has explicit XOR and biconditional constructors. Flattening expands them using AND, OR and NOT, reusing child indices inside the resulting graph. An implication is represented through its Boolean shape; recognition as an admissible operational rule is a later responsibility. Quantifier order and lexical regions determine shared variables. A repeated spelling does not license moving a variable across an unsupported negative or modal boundary. Use explicit scope and test a split-identity case.

examples.explanation: Inspect the expanded logic and follow a shared child index.

entries.title: A store mirrors validated typed facts
entries.body: The FactStore trait offers predicate-bucket lookup, contains, insert, remove, clear, iteration, length and clone_box. The small lab implementation keeps one HashMap of HashSets; it does not duplicate the corpus in a second flat set. The KB owns admission and the assertion registry. Its with_store constructor requires an empty mirror because a preloaded typed fact lacks authoritative source support for replay. A persistent implementation also needs transaction, recovery and durability contracts beyond this in-memory exercise.

examples.explanation: Install the actual small store in a real CoreSession.
examples.run_in: Pinned local lab kit inside nix develop

entries.title: One-directional matching preserves repeated bindings
entries.body: unify_facts matches a typed template against a concrete fact. Relation, arity and temporal/deontic wrapper must agree. Each PatternVar acquires a binding, and every later occurrence must match it. Substitution uses that binding map; it does not choose a new witness independently for each argument. Unspecified is an exact stored value, not a wildcard. Generated symbols, constants and numeric bit patterns retain their distinct types. Groundness validation rejects template variables or placeholders at stored-fact ingress.

examples.explanation: A shared variable requires the same entity in both places.

entries.title: Indexes narrow candidates; rules still need work
entries.body:
Predicate lookup narrows the store bucket. Matching, rule conditions, event-role joins and recursive subgoals can still generate substantial work. The lab logs actual store calls and recorder event counts while adding unrelated computer records. Those counts are interface observations, not a claim that the whole query runs in constant time. Read SearchPass, Candidate, Unification, RuleCondition, RuleFire and DepthBound events to locate effort before changing an index or budget.

The KB also maintains argument-position buckets keyed by relation, place and typed value. The anchored witness path can choose a small bound-argument bucket; unbound or unspecified arguments cannot narrow it. When equality classes are active, this path falls back so a raw-value index cannot silently omit equivalent terms. Predicate signatures and declared argument sorts are admission/type checks, not interchangeable query indexes.

examples.explanation: A multi-hop example appears in the Store and search unit.

entries.title: The registry owns support; derived caches do not
entries.body: Two independent source IDs can support the same fact or canonical rule. Deduplicating a stored conclusion must preserve both sources. Withdrawal rebuilds from surviving authoritative assertions and invalidates materialization and cached consequences; deleting a displayed row without replay is insufficient. An old proof keeps its original revision and citations. Query-local compute memos, proof references, persistent assertion IDs and any retained predicate caches have different lifetimes.

entries.title: Rule conditions and existential heads play different roles
entries.body:
Admitted universal rules are templates. Condition-side variables must be joined consistently; a successful condition can license head facts and generated witnesses. A head existential may depend on the universal variables used by that head. Its typed identity includes that dependency, so two owners can receive different generated computers. Canonical template deduplication must retain every source citation. The browser exposes public registration records and recorded rule events; private Rust template fields are not silently reconstructed.

Selective materialization first checks whether rules and their dependencies can be projected to a finite surface relation. Event-role groups can be regrouped when their event identity is local to one atom. Arbitrary existential term generation is not a finite Datalog closure. Eligible relations are completed in stratum order; an incomplete extension must not be used as evidence for a negative answer. Inspect the completed/refused report and retain backward search where saturation is unsupported.

examples.explanation: Inspect different owner-dependent witnesses in the native lab.

entries.title: A witness name is a display, not its identity
entries.body: Retain the typed witness term and origin when comparing bindings. A dependent Skolem term includes its argument dependencies; a constant that happens to have a similar printed name is still a constant. Two separate existential goals can use different witnesses. Sharing a named variable across conditions requires one joined binding. Collection APIs return a complete result or an explicit unavailability; counting a partial exploration would manufacture a total.

examples.explanation: Inspect the typed generated witness, rather than comparing only its printed name.

entries.title: A proof is a graph with actual back-references
entries.body:
ProofTrace stores a steps array and a root. Children reference earlier or shared proof steps. ProofRef carries a child pointing at an already recorded successful derivation, avoiding repeated expansion. Several parents can refer to one node; a tree rendering would duplicate it visually. Asserted and derived steps carry source or rule citations. The proof certifies its recorded result and inputs; failed candidates and search chronology belong in execution replay. A truncated event recorder and an incomplete query are separate states.

The pinned implementation caps a proof at 100,000 steps and refuses a certificate that exceeds its construction limit. Formula-evaluation exhaustion is also non-definitive. The formal-models kit separately runs the engine’s Rust regression with an eight-step test override: the whole proof is refused, then the same query certifies after the override is removed. This exercises the guard without claiming to exhaust the production ceiling.

examples.explanation: Inspect actual references, shared incoming edges, citations and the bounded recorder control.
examples.run_in: Pinned local lab kit inside nix develop

entries.title: A cache key includes the question and its state
entries.body: A reusable result depends on the goal, binding, relevant profile, source revision and supported search context. A negative answer at a shallow search horizon must not become a timeless proof of failure. The engine records typed cache operations and scopes. This course filters those captured events, without treating a missing event as evidence that no cache exists. Duplicate rule support, source withdrawal, profile changes and new top-level compute calls test different invalidation boundaries.

entries.title: Intern locally, resolve at the boundary
entries.body: SemanticCompiler uses a per-compilation Rodeo interner. Repeated equal names return the same key within that interner; keys from different instances cannot be interpreted without their own table. The semantic formula tree carries interned keys, while flattening resolves them into owned strings in LogicBuffer. Interning reduces repeated internal name storage, but it does not make all downstream strings or serializations free. The runtime lab uses the actual public interner and observes the boundary.

entries.title: Borrowed parsing input and owned syntax coexist
entries.body: pest parsing borrows the source while recognizing it. The public KR parser tree owns strings, Boxes and Vecs and remains valid after the input String is dropped. It is not the retired parser’s arena representation. Flat arrays use integer edges to avoid pointer-shaped transport, but a Vec still owns its allocation. The native experiment drops input text, compiles the owned AST and measures the resulting allocations with the same allocator instrumentation used in Integrate.

entries.title: Graph sharing does not imply shared allocation
entries.body: LogicBuffer has a nodes vector and root indices. Binary connectives reference two child indices; quantifiers reference their body; CountNode contains a variable, a count and a body index. The count is not an edge. split_roots preserves every node index by cloning the full nodes vector into each single-root buffer. Unreachable sibling nodes remain inert. The runtime lab confirms separate allocations, owned clones and JSON round-trip equality; JSON size is not a canonical-ABI cost measurement.

examples.explanation: Follow CountNode’s body edge without treating the integer count as an index.

entries.title: Resources stay with their owning component store
entries.body: The pinned component exports engine and authorizer session resources. A host instantiates the component, calls a constructor, invokes methods through that resource, and drops it through the owning store. A resource handle is not a portable assertion ID or a serializable KB snapshot. Typed logic, verdicts and proofs are values crossing the interface; host traps are outside ordinary returned error variants. Native and browser surfaces share CoreSession but have different transport and host capabilities. Inspect the actual component artifact before selecting bindings.

entries.title: Separate an encoding test from an implementation theorem
entries.body: An application counterexample tests a chosen formalization. A metamorphic test checks a relation between executions. An independent finite oracle compares behavior inside an explicit domain. A Lean theorem establishes its stated model proposition. A production extraction receipt must connect particular source bytes, tooling and a proved component contract. None alone certifies every parser, compiler, host, data source and application requirement. Name the proposition and boundary before saying a system is verified.

entries.title: Make the independent oracle small enough to inspect
entries.body: The original finite lab uses three names, unary dog/animal/alive relations, two fixed positive acyclic rules and six possible base facts. It enumerates all 64 base sets, computes an independent Boolean fixed point, and compares all nine named queries with Nibli. The oracle shares neither engine parser nor unifier nor search. It also compares recorded/plain decisions and tests reorder, consistent rename and duplicate-source transformations. These checks cover that exact fragment; they do not cover negation, equality, existential heads, arithmetic or arbitrary rules.

examples.explanation: Run 576 oracle decisions, 576 recorded/plain comparisons and 192 transformation checks.
examples.run_in: Pinned local lab kit inside nix develop

entries.title: A useful negative control can falsify the claim
entries.body: A happy path satisfying two conditions cannot distinguish AND from OR. A one-condition input can. A wrong fixed-point oracle that omits a rule edge must fail a case that needs the edge. Consistent renaming should preserve identity relationships; renaming just one occurrence deliberately changes the problem. Fuzzing explores many inputs and mutation checks probe test sensitivity, but neither automatically supplies a semantic oracle or proof. Preserve the failing input, profile, engine pin and minimized explanation before repairing it.

entries.title: Check the models that actually ran
entries.body: The formal-models lab requires Lean to be present, runs the six pinned top-level Lean files and records their source hashes and the observed Lean version. These cover Combiner, RuleFiring, Scc, Stratification, Trace and Unify models. The engine’s default shell currently supplies Lean 4.28.0; the separate production-extraction project pins its own toolchain. A successful process must not be inferred from a missing-tool skip. Read the exact model definitions and hypotheses before applying a theorem to a different implementation.

examples.explanation: Check model files and inspect the current source-bound obligation inventory.
examples.run_in: Pinned local lab kit inside nix develop

entries.title: Read the current source-bound obligation inventory
entries.body: At the selected engine revision, coverage.toml declares certified_target = "none". It separately inventories reification, resolution, lowering, quotation identity, ingress, stratification, SCC work and evaluation boundaries, with component proof work where available. Production extraction uses pinned Rust-extraction tooling and Lean, distinct from the top-level model check. A receipt must match the source and toolchain it describes; editing a coverage table or finding a theorem name does not establish implementation refinement. The companion’s model lab reads that inventory but does not issue a production extraction receipt.

entries.title: Compare the same inputs across surfaces
entries.body: A native/browser comparison needs the same engine revision, source order, profile, operation and typed result. Compare error class, Unknown reason and resource kind as well as TRUE/FALSE. A browser-only missing capability is a platform difference to explain. The course fixture harness runs authored observations natively, while browser journeys repeat selected operations through the real worker. The finite lab compares recorded and unrecorded native paths; that alone is not a browser parity result.
